questions.q: A circular loop of radius $R$ is carrying current $iA$. The ratio of magnetic field at the centre of circular loop and at a distance $R$ from the center of the loop on its axis is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The magnitude of magnetic field at the centre of loop is

${B}_{1 } = {B}_{centre } = \dfrac{{μ}_{∘}i}{2R} \ldots \left(1\right)$

~

The magnitude of magnetic field at a point at a distance $x$ from the centre along axis of loop is

${B}_{axis } = $\dfrac{{μ}_{∘}iR^{2}}{2\left(R^{2} + x^{2}\right)\dfrac{3}{2}}

${B}_{2 } = $\dfrac{{μ}_{∘}iR^{2}}{2 $\$left(2\dfrac{3}{2}\right)$R^{3}} \ldots \left(2\right)$~ ~ $( \text{since}x = R )$

Dividing equation 1 by equation 2, we get

$\dfrac{B1}{B2} =$=2\sqrt{2}: 1$

questions.q: A proton, a deuteron and an $\alpha$-particle with same kinetic energy enter into a uniform magnetic field at right angle to magnetic field. The ratio of the radii of their respective circular paths is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Radius of circular& path in magnetic field is given by&

$R = \dfrac{mv}{qB} = \dfrac{m\left(\sqrt{2\left(KE\right)}\right)}{qB\sqrt{m}} ∝ \dfrac{m}{q}$

${R}_{P}: {R}_{D}: {R}_{α} = \dfrac{1}{1}: \dfrac{2}{1}: \dfrac{4}{2} = 1: \sqrt{2}: 1$

Find the magnetic field at point $P$ due to a straight line segment $AB$ of length $6$ cm carrying a current of $5A .$ (See figure) \left({μ}_{0} = 4\pi \times {10}^{- 7}{NA}^{- 2}\right)$

questions.q:
An electron, moving along the $x -$ axis with an initial energy of $100eV,$ enters a region of magnetic field $\overset{→}{B} = \left(1.5 \times {10}^{- 3}T\right)\overset{^}{k}$ at S (see figure). The field extends between $x = 0$ and $x = 2cm .$ The electron is detected at the point $Q$ on a screen placed $8$ cm away from the point $S .$ The distance d between $P$ and $Q$ (on the screen) is:
(electron’s charge $1.6 \times {10}^{- 19}C$ , mass of electron $= 9.1 \times {10}^{- 31}kg$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$R = \dfrac{mV}{qB}$
$= \dfrac{\sqrt{2m ( K . E )}}{qB}$
\left\{mV = \sqrt{2mK . E}\right\}$
$= \dfrac{\sqrt{2 \times 9.1 \times {10}^{- 31} \times 100 \times 1.6 \times {10}^{- 19}}}{1.6 \times {10}^{- 19} \times 1.5 \times {10}^{- 3}}$
$= 2.248cm \approx 2.25cm$

$sin ⁡ \theta = \dfrac{2}{2.248} = 0.89$
$PA = R\left(1 - cos ⁡ \theta\right) = 1.22cm$
$AB = 6tan ⁡ \theta = 11.71cm$
$d = PA + AB = 12.93cm

questions.q: Two long current carrying conductors are placed parallel to each other at a distance of $8$ cm between them. The magnitude of magnetic field produced at mid-point between the two conductors due to current flowing in them is $300\mu T$. The equal current flowing in the two conductors is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Magnetic field in parallel wires is given by& $B = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}I}{2\pid}$

At midway,~$\text{distance} = \dfrac{d}{2}$

$∵ \dfrac{{μ}_{0}I}{\dfrac{2\pid}{2}} \times 2 = B$

$⇒ \dfrac{\mu0}{π} \times \dfrac{2I}{d} = B$

$⇒ \dfrac{4 \times {10}^{- 7} \times 2I}{0 . 08} = 300 \times {10}^{- 6}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{3 \times {10}^{- 4} \times 0 . 08}{2 \times 4 \times {10}^{- 7}} = 30A$

As ${B}_{net} \ne 0$,& so& the wires are carrying current in opposite direction. &

questions.q: Radiation, with wavelength $6561Å$ falls on a metal surface to produce photoelectrons. The electrons are made to enter a uniform magnetic field of $3 \times {10}^{- 4}T$ . If the radius of the largest circular path followed by the electrons is $10$ mm , the work function of the metal is close to:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$K{E}_\max = E - ϕ$
$= \dfrac{12400}{\lambda\left(inÅ\right)} - ϕ$ (in eV)
$∴ r = \dfrac{\sqrt{2mKE}}{eB}$
$K{E}_\max = \dfrac{r^{2}e^{2}B^{2}}{2m}$ (in J)
$= \dfrac{r^{2}eB^{2}}{2m}$ (in eV)
$∴ ϕ = \dfrac{12400}{6556} - \dfrac{r^{2}eB^{2}}{2m}$
$= 1.1eV$

questions.q: A particle having the same charge as of electron moves in a circular path of radius $0.5$ cm under the influence of a magnetic field of $0.5T .$ If an electric field of 100 V/m makes it to move in a straight path, then the mass of the particle is (Given charge of electron $= 1.6 \times {10}^{- 19}C$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Force to due to magnetic field

$F = evB = \dfrac{mv^{2}}{R}$

with electric field also, net force is zero.

$∴ eE = evB$

$⇒ E = vB$

$E = \dfrac{eBR}{m} . B$

$⇒ m = \dfrac{eB^{2}R}{E} = \dfrac{1.6 \times {10}^{- 19} \times {\left(0.5\right)}^{2} . \left(0.5 \times {10}^{- 2}\right)}{100}kg$

$= 2.0 \times {10}^{- 24}kg$

questions.q:
A current of $1 . 5A$ is flowing through a triangle, of side $9$ cm each. The magnetic field at the centroid of the triangle is :

questions.solution:

${B}_{net} = 3{B}_{1} = 3 \times {10}^{- 5}T ⊗$

questions.q: A particle of charge& $q$ and mass~$m$ is moving with a velocity~$- v\overset{^}{i} ( v \ne 0 )$ towards a large screen placed in the~$Y - Z$ plane at distance d. If there is magnetic field~$\overset{→}{B} = {B}_{0}\overset{^}{k},$ the minimum value of~$v$& for which the particle will not hit the screen is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The radius of circular path in given magnetic field is

$r = d = \dfrac{mv}{q{B}_{0}}$

so~$v = \dfrac{q{B}_{0}d}{m}$

questions.q:
The electric current in a circular coil of& $2$ turns produces a magnetic induction ${B}_{1}$~at its centre. The coil is unwound and is rewound into a circular coil of~$5$ turns and the same current produces a magnetic induction ${B}_{2}$~at its centre.
The ratio of $\dfrac{B2}{B1}$& is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Magnetic field on the centre of a circular current coil is given by& $B = \dfrac{N{μ}_{0}i}{2R}$, here,~$N$~is number of turns,~$i$~is current and~$R$~is radius of loop.

Now, for,~$N = 2$, magnetic field,~${B}_{1} = \dfrac{{N}_{1}{μ}_{0}i}{2{R}_{1}}$

For~${N}_{2} = 5$

Radius of coil~$= {R}_{2} = \dfrac{{N}_{1} \times {R}_{1}}{N2}$

Magnetic field,~${B}_{2} = \dfrac{{N}_{2}{μ}_{0}i}{2{R}_{2}}$

Thus, the ratio is~$\dfrac{B2}{B1} = \dfrac{N2}{N1}\dfrac{R1}{R2} = \dfrac{N2}{N1} \times \dfrac{N2}{N1}$

$\dfrac{B2}{B1} = \dfrac{25}{4}$

questions.q:
Match List I with List II

List − I
(Current configuration)		 List − II
(Magnetic field at point $O$)
A I. ${B}_{0} = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}I}{4\pir} [ \pi + 2 ]$
B II. ${B}_{0} = \dfrac{\mu0}{4}\dfrac{I}{r}$
C III. ${B}_{0} = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}I}{2\pir} [ \pi - 1 ]$
D IV. ${B}_{0} = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}I}{4\pir} [ \pi + 1 ]$

Choose the correct answer from the option given below:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
(A)

Here net magnetic field will be sum of magnetic field due to straight wires& $ab, de$~and due to loop~$bcd$.

So,~${B}_{ab} = \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} = {B}_{de}$~(directed out of the plane in both cases)

${B}_{bcd} = \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} ( 2\pi )$~(in the plane)

Thus, magnetic field at $O$ is

${B}_{O} = - \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} + \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} ( 2\pi ) - \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r}$

${B}_{O} = \dfrac{\mu0}{2\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} ( \pi - 1 )$~ (III)

(B)

Here net magnetic field will be sum of magnetic field due to straight wires~$ab, de$~and semicircular arc~$bcd$.

${B}_{ab} = \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} = {B}_{de}$~(directed out of the plane in both cases)

${B}_{bcd} = \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} ( \pi )$~(out of the plane)

Thus, net magnetic field at $O$ is

${B}_{O} = \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} + \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} ( \pi ) + \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r}$

${B}_{0} = \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} ( \pi + 2 )$~(I)

(C)

Here net magnetic field will be sum of magnetic field due to straight wires~$ab, de$~and due to loop~$bcd$.

${B}_{ab} = \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r}$~(directed in~the plane)

${B}_{bcd} = \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} ( \pi )$~(in the plane)

${B}_{de} = 0$~(passing through the axis)

Thus, magnetic field at $O$ is

${B}_{O} = \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} ( \pi + 1 )$~ (IV)

(D)

Here net magnetic field will be sum of magnetic field due to straight wires~$ab, de$~and due to loop~$bcd$.

${B}_{ab} = 0 = {B}_{de}$~(passing through the axis)

${B}_{bcd} = \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} ( \pi )$~(out of the plane)

Thus, magnetic field at $O$ is

${B}_{O} = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}I}{4r}$& (II).

A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

questions.q: The magnetic field at the centre of a circular coil of radius $r$, due to current I flowing through it, is $B$. The magnetic field at a point along the axis at a distance $\dfrac{r}{2}$ from the centre is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Magnetic field at the centre of the circle is,& $B = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}i}{2R}$

Magnetic field at the point on the axis is,~

${B}_{2} = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}iR^{2}}{2\left(R^{2} + x^{2}\right)\dfrac{3}{2}} ⇒ {B}_{2} = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}iR^{2}}{2\left(R^{2} + \left(\dfrac{R}{2}\right)2\right)\dfrac{3}{2}} ⇒ {B}_{2} = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}i}{2\left(\dfrac{5}{4}\right)\dfrac{3}{2}R} = \left(\dfrac{2}{5}\right)3B$

questions.q: A wire $A$, bent in the shape of an arc of a circle, carrying a current of $2A$ and having radius $2$ cm and another wire $B$, also bent in the shape of an arc of a circle, carrying a current of $3A$ and having radius of $4\text{cm}$, are placed as shown in the figure. The ratio of the magnetic fields due to the wires $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ at the common centre $\text{O}$ is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given,

Current in the arc& $A$~is~${i}_{1} = 2A$

Current in the arc~$B$~is~${i}_{2} = 3A$

Radius of arc~$A$~is~${R}_{1} = 2cm$

Radius of arc~$B$~is~${R}_{2} = 4cm$

Magnetic field at the centre of circular current carrying arc is given by

${B}_{C} = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}i}{4\piR}\left(\theta\right) . . . ( 1 )$~

Where,~$\theta$~is the~angle subtended~at centre.

Magnetic field at the centre due to arc $A$~and~$B$~is given by~

${B}_{A} = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}{i}_{1}}{4{πR}_{1}} \lleft(2\pi - \dfrac{π}{2}\right) . . . \left($2\right)$

${B}_{B} = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}{i}_{2}}{4{πR}_{2}} \lleft(2\pi - \dfrac{π}{3}\right) . . . \left($3\right)$

Dividing equation (2) by (1), we get

$⇒ \dfrac{BA}{BB} = \dfrac{i1}{i2} \times \dfrac{{R}_{2}\left(2\pi - \dfrac{π}{2}\right)}{{R}_{1}\left(2\pi - \dfrac{π}{3}\right)}$

$⇒ \dfrac{BA}{BB} = \dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{4}{2} \times \dfrac{3\pi}{2} \times \dfrac{3}{5\pi}$

$⇒ \dfrac{BA}{BB} = \dfrac{6}{5}$

questions.q: The electric current in a circular coil of four turns produces a magnetic induction $32T$ at its centre. The coil is unwound and is rewound into a circular coil of single turn, the magnetic induction at the centre of the coil by the same current will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Magnetic field at the centre of the coil is given by,& $B = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}i}{2R}$.

Now in the first case:

$B = 4 \left(\dfrac{{μ}_{0}i}{2R}\right)

and for the second case:

$B ' = $\dfrac{{μ}_{0}i}{2R '}.

As the length of the wire will remain same, therefore

$2\piR ' = 4\left($2\piR\right) ⇒ R ' = 4R$

Hence, required ratio will be

\dfrac{B '}{B} = \dfrac{R}{4R^{'}} = \dfrac{1}{16}

$⇒ B ' = 2T$

questions.q: A thin ring of $10$ cm radius carries a uniformly distributed charge. The ring rotates at a constant angular speed of $40\pirads^{- 1}$ about its axis, perpendicular to its plane. Is the magnetic field its centre is $3.8 \times {10}^{- 9}T$ , then the charge carried by the ring is close to \left({\mu}_{0} = 4\pi \times {10}^{- 7}N / A^{2}\right) .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$i = \dfrac{q}{t} = \dfrac{q}{2\pi / \omega} = \dfrac{q\omega}{2\pi}$
$B = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}i}{2R} = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}q\omega}{4\piR}$
$\dfrac{4\pi \times {10}^{- 7} \times q \times 40\pi}{4\pi \times ( 0.1 )} = 3.8 \times {10}^{- 9}$
$q \times \left(400\pi\right) = 3.8 \times {10}^{- 2}$
$q = 3 \times {10}^{- 5}$ C

questions.q: The magnetic field at the center of current carrying circular loop is ${B}_{1}$. The magnetic field at a distance of $\sqrt{3}$ times radius of the given circular loop from the center on its axis is ${B}_{2}$. The value of $\dfrac{B1}{B2}$ will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Magnetic field at the centre of the loop i.e.& ${B}_{1} = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}i}{2R}$

Magnetic field on the axis of the loop is,

${B}_{2} = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}iR^{2}}{2\left(R^{2} + x^{2}\right)\dfrac{3}{2}} = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}i \times R^{2}}{2\left(R^{2} + 3R^{2}\right)\dfrac{3}{2}}= \dfrac{{μ}_{0}i \times R^{2}}{2 \times 8R^{3}}= \dfrac{{μ}_{0}i}{2 \times 8R}$

Therefore, the ratio~$\dfrac{B1}{B2} = \dfrac{8}{1}$

questions.q: ${B}_{X}$ and ${B}_{Y}$ are the magnetic field at the centre of two coils of two coils $X$ and $Y$ respectively, each carrying equal current. If coil $X$ has $200$ turns and $20$ cm radius and coil $Y$ has $400$ turns and $20$ cm radius, the ratio of ${B}_{X}$ and ${B}_{Y}$ is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Magnetic field at the& centre of a single coil is& $B = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}i}{2R}$

If~$N$~number of loops are kept closely~$B = N \left(\dfrac{{μ}_{0}i}{2R}\right)

Therefore,

\dfrac{Bx}{By} = \dfrac{Nx}{Ny}

$⇒ \dfrac{Bx}{By} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$

questions.q: Two $10$ cm long, straight wires, each carrying a current of $5A$ are kept parallel to each other. If each wire experienced a force of ${10}^{- 5}N$, then separation between the wires is _____~$cm .$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given:& $F = {10}^{- 5}N$

Force between wires~$\dfrac{F}{l} = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}{i}_{1}{i}_{2}}{2\pid}$, where,~$d$~is separation between them.

~$⇒ \dfrac{10- 5}{0 . 1} = \dfrac{2 \times {10}^{- 7} \times 25}{d}$

$⇒ d = 50 \times {10}^{- 3}m = 5cm$

questions.q: The magnetic field at the centre of a wire loop formed by two semicircular wires of radii ${R}_{1} = 2\pim$ and ${R}_{2} = 4\pim$ carrying current $I = 4A$ as per figure given below is $\alpha \times {10}^{- 7}T$. The value of $\alpha$ is _____. (Centre $O$ is common for all segments)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From the figure, it is evident that the magnetic field at $O$ due to the straight portion of the loop is zero, only the contributions from the circular parts survive.

Also, the direction of the magnetic field due to the circular loops can be determined by the right-hand corkscrew rule.

Hence, the net magnetic field at $O$ can be calculated as follows:

$\begin{cases}B & = & \dfrac{{μ}_{0}i}{2{R}_{2}}\left(\dfrac{π}{2\pi}\right) ⊗ + \dfrac{{μ}_{0}i}{2{R}_{1}}\left(\dfrac{π}{2\pi}\right) ⊗ \\ & = & \left(\dfrac{{μ}_{0}i}{4{R}_{2}} + \dfrac{{μ}_{0}i}{4{R}_{1}}\right) ⊗ \\ & = & \dfrac{4\pi \times {10}^{- 7} \times 4}{4 \times 4\pi} + \dfrac{4\pi \times {10}^{- 7} \times 4}{4 \times 2\pi} ⊗ T \\ & = & 3 \times {10}^{- 7} ⊗ T\end{cases}$

Hence, $\alpha = 3$.

questions.q: A charge particle of $2\mu C$ accelerated by a potential difference of $100V$ enters a region of uniform magnetic field of magnitude $4mT$ at right angle to the direction of field. The charge particle completes semicircle of radius $3$ cm inside magnetic field. The mass of the charge particle is ______~$\times {10}^{- 18}kg$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As we know, radius of the circular path is given by,

$r = \dfrac{mv}{qB} = \dfrac{2mK}{qB} = \dfrac{2 \times m \times qV}{qB}$

$⇒ r^{2} = \dfrac{2mV}{qB^{2}}$

$⇒ m = \dfrac{r^{2}qB^{2}}{2V} = \dfrac{\left(3 \times {10}^{- 2}\right)2 \times \left(2 \times {10}^{- 6}\right) \times \left(4 \times {10}^{- 3}\right)2}{2 \times 100} = 144 \times {10}^{- 18}kg$

questions.q:
A tightly wound long solenoid carries a current of 1.5 A . An electron is executing uniform circular motion inside the solenoid with a time period of 75 ns . The number of turns per metre in the solenoid is $\ldots\ldots$ -.
[Take mass of electron $\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{e}}=9 \times 10^{-31} \mathrm{~kg}$, charge of electron \left|\mathrm{q}_{\mathrm{e}}\right|=1.6 \times 10^{-19} \mathrm{C}$,  \left.\mu_0=4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \frac{\mathrm{~N}}{\mathrm{~A}^2}, 1 \mathrm{~ns}=10^{-9} \mathrm{~s}\right]$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Since time period of a revolving charge is $\frac{2 \pi m}{q B}$
Where $\mathrm{B}=$ magnetic field
due to a solenoid $=\mu_0 \mathrm{nI}\begin{aligned}
& \therefore \mathrm{T}=\frac{2 \pi \mathrm{~m}}{\mathrm{q}\left(\mu_0 \mathrm{nI}\right)} \\
& 75 \times 10^{-9}=\frac{(2 \pi)\left(9 \times 10^{-31}\right)}{1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times \mathrm{n} \times 1.5} \\
& \mathrm{~N}=250
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The current of $5A$ flows in a square loop of sides $1m$ is placed in air. The magnetic field at the centre of the loop is $X\sqrt{2} \times {10}^{- 7}T$. The value of $X$ is _________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Magnetic field at the centre of the square loop is given by,

$B = 4 $\$left[\dfrac{{μ}_{0}I}{4\pid} \left($sin45 ° + sin45 °\right)\right]$, where $d$ is perpendicular distance of the centre to one of its sides.

$⇒ B = 4 $\times \dfrac{{μ}_{0} \times 5}{4\pi \times \dfrac{1}{2}} \left(\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

$= 4 \times {10}^{- 7} \times5 \times2 \times \sqrt{2}$

$= 40\sqrt{2} \times {10}^{- 7}T$

$
